| Source | Finding (terse) | Verified? | Classification | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Codex | Trigger-2 fires on ANY `epm:failure` in history (incl. one BEFORE the ladder launches), not on a post-exhaustion gate re-trip | ✓ | Real-blocking | Blocking |
| Claude | MF#1–7 all landed; 20/20 new + 57/57 existing tests pass; ruff + workflow_lint clean; predicate pure | ✓ (but tests do not cover the ordering case) | Real-nonblocking (does not refute the Codex finding) | Non-blocking |

### Rationale
Codex is right; Claude's PASS rested on a test suite with a coverage gap exactly where the bug lives.

I reran Codex's repro verbatim against the worktree code. With `events = [epm:failure (pre-ladder), progress "Option A", progress "Option B"]` and a 2-option ladder, `circuit_breaker_should_fire(events, plan_text, K=4)` returns the `enumerated_fallback_exhausted` fire dict — it must return `None`, because the gate did NOT re-trip after the ladder was exhausted. The defect is at `src/explore_persona_space/task_workflow.py:1114`:

```python
if not any(e.get("kind", "") == "epm:failure" for e in events):
    return None
```

This is an existence check over the WHOLE history, not a "re-tripped after the last option launch" check. It under-implements trigger-2's defining half. The plan v2 spec is explicit (`tasks/running/718/plans/v2.md`, §5.1 lines 155-161): trigger-2 fires only when "EVERY named alternative in that ladder has been LAUNCHED, AND the SAME gate still trips ... 'Tried to exhaustion' = every named alternative in the ladder has been launched AND the same gate has re-tripped." The SKILL.md prose shipped in this same PR agrees verbatim (`.claude/skills/issue/SKILL.md` lines 3781-3783: "scans ... `epm:failure` markers re-tripping the SAME gate. When EVERY option in the ladder has been launched AND the same gate still trips → fire"). The implementation contradicts both registered contracts.

Impact is not cosmetic. On a false fire the orchestrator (SKILL.md Step 7, lines 3793-3798) posts `epm:strategy-pivot`, runs `task.py set-status <N> planning`, and re-invokes `/adversarial-planner`. So a stale, unrelated `epm:failure` that merely predates two option-launch progress notes can yank a healthy `/issue` session out of its crash-fix loop into a full re-plan — and the emitted `pivot_scope` string then asserts "the gate re-tripped each time," which is factually false for that event stream. This is the gate misfiring on its own primary trigger, on the production recovery path, which makes it Real & blocking.

Why Claude missed it: tests (d) and (e) are the only trigger-2 cases. (d) interleaves a failure AFTER each launch (passes even with the buggy existence check); (e) tests an INCOMPLETE ladder. Neither exercises a COMPLETE ladder whose only failure PRECEDES the launches — the exact hole the bug occupies. Claude verified "20/20 pass" honestly, but the suite cannot catch this class, and Claude did not independently construct the adversarial ordering case. Codex did, with a concrete repro, and was correct.

The fix is localized and mechanizable (as Codex specified): require an `epm:failure` indexed AFTER the last matched option-launch note before firing trigger-2, and add a regression test with `[pre-ladder failure, Option A, Option B]` asserting `circuit_breaker_should_fire(...) is None`. This is a revise-then-merge, not a redesign — but it must land before merge because the predicate is the single source of truth both the tests and the orchestrator consult, and it currently produces wrong fires on the launch path.
